issue.title: Turn every red sase workflow green
issue.description: On sase-org/sase, Master Gate, Full CI, CI Telemetry, and Publish are green at the master tip, and CI on the open release-please PR is green at its head. Each one is the latest run of its workflow, completed with success on a SHA at or after the last fix, with no in-scope job cancelled or skipped. Green evidence is published as ci_evidence. Otherwise, after a very large and documented effort, a research-sidecar report says exactly what is still needed. Then the land agent closes phase sase-1rq.2 of epic sase-1rq.

issue.title: Stop the coverage-contexts lane crashing on global disk patches
issue.description: coverage-contexts: CI Telemetry's coverage-contexts job dies in a pytest-xdist INTERNALERROR. test_inflight_handler_does_no_synchronous_disk_or_proc_store_work patches os.stat and pathlib.Path methods globally with a raising stub. Coverage's ctrace tracer then calls os.path.exists while the patch is active and hits the assertion inside the tracer. Scope that guard so it only sees the code under test. Audit the other tests that globally patch os, os.path, or pathlib with raising stubs for the same hazard, and prove the cov-contexts lane passes on the affected modules.

issue.title: Make the test-cost lane finish inside its 180-minute timeout
issue.description: test-cost: CI Telemetry's test-cost job is cancelled at its unchanged 180-minute timeout, about 93% through 60,399 items on 3 workers (run 42347892210). Full CI's test (3.12) runs the same items on the same 3 workers in about 61 minutes, so the cost lane's own plugins (cost recorder plus --sase-detect-global-leaks / --sase-fail-on-global-leaks) add roughly 3x overhead. Find and remove that overhead. Then make the whole recipe pass: the run, test_cost_report, and check_test_cost_budgets. Change no timeouts, budgets, or leak gates.

issue.title: Make the contention-test lane survive and pass
issue.description: contention: CI Telemetry's contention-test job (SASE_CONTENTION_REPEAT=1 just test-contention, 26 workers on 2 pinned CPUs) prints nothing for about 20 minutes. Then the runner gets a shutdown signal, on both the 06:54 and 13:48 UTC runs on 2026-11-07. The lane has never produced a tally in CI. Find out why the runner dies (memory or disk exhaustion is the lead) and fix it without changing the width, repeat count, CPU pinning, or timeout. Then make the single repeat pass: root-cause each failure under contention, or quarantine proven flakes.
